name: Keshi Is Throwing a Party
description: Keshi is throwing a party and he wants everybody in the party to be happy. He has $$$n$$$ friends. His $$$i$$$-th friend has $$$i$$$ dollars. If you invite the $$$i$$$-th friend to the party, he will be happy only if at most $$$a_i$$$ people in the party are strictly richer than him and at most $$$b_i$$$ people are strictly poorer than him. Keshi wants to invite as many people as possible. Find the maximum number of people he can invite to the party so that every invited person would be happy.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ $$$(1\le t\le 10^4)$$$ — the number of test cases. The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ $$$(1\le n\le 2 \cdot 10^5)$$$ — the number of Keshi's friends. The $$$i$$$-th of the following $$$n$$$ lines contains two integers $$$a_i$$$ and $$$b_i$$$ $$$(0 \le a_i, b_i \lt n)$$$. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case print the maximum number of people Keshi can invite.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1610C — Keshi Is Throwing a Party [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
